column1: # Linorobot2 Cockpit ESP32 partition table (4 MB flash)
# Identical to the Arduino default table except for the `env` partition carved
# out of the front of the filesystem area. That partition holds the U-Boot-style
# environment block: the Wi-Fi credentials and the address of the machine
# running micro_ros_agent live THERE
# Keeping them out of the image is what makes firmware/prebuilt/ worth shipping.
# A binary with an SSID compiled into it only ever works on one LAN
# would have to rebuild -- and a prebuilt image that requires a toolchain is no
# prebuilt image at all. With the env split out
#     esptool write_flash 0x3ff000 env.bin
# and reflashing the application never disturbs the keys
# write_flash 0x10000 firmware.bin` does not touch this region.
# `adclut` holds the ESP32 ADC linearisation table generated by
# firmware/adc_calibrate: sector 0 is a header (magic
# CRC32) and sectors 1-2 are 4096 int16 entries. The tool writes it in 512-byte
# blocks and the firmware reads it back through esp_partition_mmap
# side ever holds the table in RAM.
# 2026-09-20: the app slots grew from 1280 KB to 1984 KB each
# to the LAST sector of flash.
# The old table gave each app slot 1280 KB and left a 1456 KB `spiffs` region
# that nothing in this project has ever used -- no SPIFFS
# call. Meanwhile esp32_lyrical had reached 85% of its slot
# that used to be compiled in or out are all compiled in now. Dead space on one
# side of the flash and a ceiling on the other.
# `env` sits at the very top (0x3ff000) rather than after the app slots so that
# this is the LAST time it moves: the apps can grow into the middle without
# touching it again. It matches the RP2 boards
